messages.content: I feel like the main body text is so soft tiny and gets lost. I still want a professional look but make more impactful

I’ll inspect the app structure and typography styles first, then adjust the body copy scale/weight in the smallest scoped place that affects the main experience.This is a small static site, so the typography is likely centralized in `styles.css`. I’m reading the CSS and representative pages to see whether “main body text” is global or page-specific.The body is currently set to Jost at weight `300`, with many paragraphs at `17px` and muted color. That explains the soft feel; I’m going to lift the default body weight and strengthen paragraph/lede sizing and contrast without making the brand look heavy.I found a few page-specific styles too, especially on the workshops page, so I’m treating both the global paragraph system and those local overrides. The intent is stronger readability across pages, not just one section.Next I’m editing CSS values only: default text weight, muted color contrast, paragraph sizes, and a few card/list overrides. I’m keeping headings and layout intact so the change feels more polished rather than redesigned.The global pass is done. I’m making a small second pass on the workshop-only stylesheet because it had its own copy rules that would otherwise stay softer than the rest of the site.The typography edits are in place. I’m checking the diff now for accidental layout churn and to make sure the changes are limited to text weight, size, line-height, and contrast.The diff is clean and scoped. I noticed an untracked `.codex/` directory already present, but I didn’t touch it; only `styles.css` and `workshop.html` were changed.Updated the main typography to feel more substantial while staying professional.

Changed:
- Raised default body weight from `300` to `400`
- Darkened the muted body text color
- Increased paragraph/lede/list/card copy sizes across the site
- Tightened line-height slightly so larger text still feels polished
- Strengthened lighter text on dark sections
- Matched the workshop page’s inline styles to the new stronger text system

Files changed: `styles.css`, `workshop.html`

Verification: `git diff --check` passed.\

I also see uncommitted changes in `styles.css` and `workshop.html`, so I’ll preserve those and deploy the current working tree as-is.There’s no Netlify CLI installed and no local `.netlify` site link. I’m checking whether this repo has a git remote configured for Netlify-triggered deploys, which is usually the cleanest path for static sites like this.The only configured remote is GitHub, on branch `current-github-main`. I’m going to inspect the modified files before committing so I don’t accidentally include local tool files or unrelated generated content.The tracked changes are typography/contrast tweaks only; `.codex/` is local agent metadata and won’t be included. I’ll commit the two site files, then push the current branch to `origin` so Netlify can pick up the connected GitHub deploy.`git diff --check` is clean, so there are no whitespace errors in the modified files. I’m committing just `styles.css` and `workshop.html` now.The deploy path is blocked at the git step: this session has read-only access to `.git`, so `git commit` cannot create `.git/index.lock`. I’m doing one quick check to make sure nothing was partially staged, then I’ll give you the exact commands to run locally.I couldn’t push it from this session because `.git` is read-only here, so `git commit` failed before it could stage anything. No partial lock file was left behind.

Run these from the repo to push the current site changes and trigger Netlify via GitHub:

```bash
git add styles.css workshop.html
git commit -m "Improve site readability"
git push origin current-github-main:main
```

I left `.codex/` untracked and out of the commit.\
